narration_ml: Section 4-inte adisthanathil, Diversion of Income by Overriding Title matrum Application of Income thammilulla vyathyasam thirichariyunnath income tax computation-il valare pradhanappetta oru karyamanu.

card.title: Scope of Income Diversion Doctrine
lines: Section 4 governs the chargeability of income based on its accrual or receipt.
Diversion occurs when income is redirected by a legal obligation before reaching the assessee.
Application refers to the use of income after it has accrued to the assessee.
The distinction determines whether an amount is excluded from Total Income.

narration_ml: Oru legal obligation vazhi income assessee-yude kayyil ethunnathinu munpu thanne maatti vidunnathineyanu Diversion by Overriding Title ennu vilikkunnath.

card.title: Criteria for Overriding Title
lines: Requires an enforceable legal or statutory obligation.
The obligation must override the assessee's title to the income.
The income must be diverted at source before accrual.
Self-imposed conditions do not constitute an overriding title.

narration_ml: Diversion of Income matrum Application of Income thammilulla pradhana vyathyasangal Point of Transfer, Nature of Obligation, Title, matrum Taxability ennivayude adisthanathil ee statutory table-il nalkiyittundu.

card.title: Statutory Distinction Matrix
lines: Comparative analysis of Diversion vs. Application.
Based on statutory principles and judicial interpretations.
Determines the ultimate tax liability under Section 4.

rows: Diverted at source before reaching the assessee.
Applied after the income reaches or accrues to the assessee.
Enforceable legal/statutory obligation overriding assessee's title.
Voluntary obligation or self-imposed condition by the assessee.
Assessee never acquires title or ownership over such income.
Assessee acquires full beneficial ownership before applying it.
Not taxable in the hands of the assessee.
Taxable in the hands of the assessee under relevant head.

narration_ml: Income-inte mel assessee-kku title labhikkunnundo illayo ennathum, athu taxable aano ennathum ee matrix-ile pradhana vyathyasangal aanu.

card.title: Ownership and Taxability Matrix
lines: Diversion results in no acquisition of title by the assessee.
Application implies full beneficial ownership prior to use.
Taxability is negated only in cases of genuine diversion.

rows: Assessee never acquires title or ownership.
Not taxable in the hands of the assessee.
Taxable in the hands of the assessee.

narration_ml: Diversion by Overriding Title vazhi maatti vidappetta income, assessee-yude Total Income-il ninnu purathakkunnathinal athinmel tax nalkendathilla.

card.title: Computation of Diverted Income
lines: Identify income subject to enforceable legal obligation.
Exclude such diverted amounts at the source of accrual.
Net income after diversion is subject to Section 4 charge.
Diverted income is not included in the assessee's tax base.

narration_ml: Application of Income-inte karyathil, assessee-kku income labhichu kazhinju mathramaanu athu upayogikkunnath, athukondu athu relevant head-il taxable aayirikkum.

card.title: Taxability of Applied Income
lines: Income reaches or accrues to the assessee first.
Subsequent disposal or application does not reduce tax liability.
Taxable under relevant head (e.g., Section 28 for business).
Full amount is included in Total Income computation.

narration_ml: CIT v. Thakar Das Bhargava case-ile precedent anusarichu, professional fees voluntary aayi charitable trust-inu nalkunnath Application of Income mathramaanu.

card.title: Precedent: CIT v. Thakar Das Bhargava
lines: Professional fees received are taxable under Section 28.
Voluntary allocation to charity is mere application of income.
Self-created desires do not constitute an overriding title.
The obligation must be external and legally enforceable.

narration_ml: Exam-il oru voluntary agreement-o self-imposed condition-o kandal athu Application of Income aayi karuthi full amount tax cheyyanam.

card.title: Common Statutory Traps
lines: Distinguish between 'at source' and 'after accrual'.
Check if the obligation is voluntary or legally mandated.
Section 28 professional earnings are often targets for this trap.
Diversion requires the assessee to never acquire title.
